A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CityGaussianV2 work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments, rendering and geometry metrics, efficiency measurements, and component ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and reports additional parallel-training comparisons in Appendix B and reconstruction failure cases in Figure 11.

M1.justification: The depth supervision, SSIM-based decomposed-gradient densification, elongation filter, parallel trimming, reduced SH degree, and quantization procedures remain unchanged. Added explanations do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three GauU-Scene scenes and MatrixCity aerial and street views, and use Rubble for the densification illustration. The added comparisons and failure cases do not introduce distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 4 evaluates 2DGS*, which directly combines 2DGS with CityGS parallel training without the proposed optimization mechanism. The original benchmark comparator set remains intact; SuGaR's replacement of OOM entries with scores changes results rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: New Table 4 introduces compressed comparisons with approximately matched Gaussian counts for CityGS and the proposed method. Table 2 also replaces the 10.9-million-Gaussian CityGS configuration with an 8.05-million configuration. Existing dataset splits, image preprocessing, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct test of naive 2DGS-plus-CityGS parallel training and comparisons controlling Gaussian count. Figure 11 adds failure cases involving road surfaces, building facades, and a spire. The existing component and gradient-source ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the claimed F1 error-bar reduction from 0.1 to 0.003 and the same uncertainty-based interpretation of gradient ablations. V2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: New Table 4 substantially expands the quality–efficiency evidence and reports 2DGS* OOM failures in four of five scenes. Existing comparisons also change materially: SuGaR's aerial OOM entries become PSNR 22.41 and F1 0.169; CityGS's GauU-Scene F1 in Table 1 changes from 0.407 to 0.453, narrowing the proposed method's advantage. The proposed method's street-view PSNR changes from 22.19 to 22.24. Revised Table 2 CityGS results use a different Gaussian count and cannot be treated as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the definitions of the covariance factors: v1 identifies R_n as scaling and S_n as rotation, while v2 reverses these roles to match the retained covariance expression. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, four contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about optimization, scalable reconstruction, compression, efficiency, and geometric evaluation. Updated comparative results do not redefine the core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly identifies compensated or constant lighting as a coverage limitation and discusses failures caused by occlusion and insufficient observations. It strengthens the rendering-speed limitation by noting that CityGS remains faster at similar Gaussian counts. The introduction also revises explanations of SuGaR's memory problems and GOF's underfitting.

D1.justification: Section 4 adds the ground-truth transformation used for ground-plane projection and specifies a timing example involving 958 views, 31.4 million points, 1080p rendering, and a 40 GB A100. Figure 3 clarifies that one Rubble block is tuned. The abstract now explicitly describes the existing project link as providing official code and demos; learning-rate guidance is merely relocated to Appendix C.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section remain unchanged, but the introduction qualifies the characterization of SuGaR: memory failure is attributed to suboptimal implementation rather than extensive mesh complexity. This is a limited refinement of positioning against prior work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose and caption revisions, moves learning-rate guidance into Appendix C, and expands the discussion. It updates the publication header and affiliations and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 4 and failure-case Figure 11, replaces SuGaR's aerial OOM placeholders with images in Figures 6 and 7, and relocates Figure 10. Existing appendix tables are renumbered and repositioned, while the overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: The comparisons at similar Gaussian counts, completed SuGaR results, and explicit failure cases and lighting limitations make the empirical evidence more informative and balanced. The gain is limited by unresolved reporting discrepancies: for example, v2 Tables 2 and 4 report 34.5 and 45.5 FPS for the Residence small model without explaining the difference.
